gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a single-cable USB-C KVM dock can run dual 4K at 60 Hz only if the laptop's USB-C port outputs DisplayPort 1.4 with DSC (Display Stream Compression). Without DSC, a DP Alt Mode link that also carries USB 3 data has room for only one 4K60 stream or two 2560×1600 streams. Docks like the iDock C20 and KD-E10 advertise both dual 4K60 over MST and 5 Gb/s USB on that same laptop cable.
standout_why: I compared five rival pages. Dock Gear HQ's built-in-KVM page (cited) and ThunderboltLaptop's dual-monitor page (cited) both cover macOS mirroring over MST and DisplayLink. Dock Gear HQ also covers base M1/M2 display limits and the iDock M10's two-cable design. ThunderboltLaptop covers M3 lid-closed operation. ChatGPT's own answer repeats the MST mirroring warning. Dock Gear HQ's best-kvm-switches-2026 page (cited) mentions DSC only for 8K/4K144 modes on the Sabrent and TESmart. Tried Tested Reviewed (rank 1) mentions DSC nowhere. None of the five says that dual 4K60 from one USB-C cable depends on the host having DSC, or that DP Alt Mode trades video lanes against USB 3 data. ThunderboltLaptop also claims that M3 Pro, M3 Max and M4 Macs 'support native dual extended via MST'. AV Access's own pages contradict that: they say macOS doesn't support USB-C MST and the M10 gets two extended screens by using two cables.
decides: This mainly affects Windows buyers. The iDock C20 ($259.99, ChatGPT's top pick) and the KD-E10 ($169.99) give two extended 4K60 screens only on a laptop whose USB-C port supports DP Alt Mode, MST and, for dual 4K60 alongside USB 3 data, DP 1.4 DSC. Older or iGPU-limited laptops will run at lower resolution or refresh, as C20 owners report seeing on the maker's page. Those buyers should either confirm DSC in their laptop's specs or pick a dock that doesn't depend on it: Thunderbolt (Sabrent), DisplayLink (StarTech 129N), or the iDock M10, which takes two uncompressed DP Alt Mode streams over two cables. For Macs this confirms ChatGPT's warning: the C20 and KD-E10 mirror. The M10 extends to two screens on M4/M5 or Pro/Max chips, and on a base M3 only with the lid closed.

findings.label: Laptop-port requirement for two extended displays
findings.value: USB-C port must support DP Alt Mode and DP MST; video input listed as 'Dual 4K@60Hz video (MST)'
findings.source_title: AV Access iDock C20 KVM Switch Docking Station
findings.note: Maker's important note 1: 'For the extended display mode on two screens, please make sure that your USB C port supports DP alt and DP MST.'

findings.label: Data rate on the laptop link alongside dual 4K60
findings.value: Up to 5 Gb/s USB data together with dual 4K UHD video over each 20 Gb/s USB-C laptop link
findings.source_title: AV Access iDock C20 KVM Switch Docking Station
findings.note: Maker copy: 'With dual 20Gbps USB C ports, iDock C20 delivers dual 4K UHD videos, data transfer up to 5Gbps'. Sending USB 3 data on the same cable needs the 2-lane DP Alt Mode split (Newnex finding below), so dual 4K60 then depends on host DSC. AV Access does not state the DSC requirement. A buyer review on the page (Matthew Wills, 2025-01-10) says one laptop's UHD graphics 'only allows for 30Hz at 4K'.

findings.note: Spec table lists Windows 'Extended' and MacBook 'Mirrored'. Maker: 'MacOS doesn't support USB-C MST'. Desktop side uses DP 1.4a and HDMI 2.0b inputs plus USB-B, so the desktop doesn't depend on DP Alt Mode.

findings.label: How it avoids MST on a Mac
findings.value: Dual-head USB-C cable (or two separate USB-C cables); two USB-C/Thunderbolt ports needed; DP Alt video 'without compression'
findings.note: Maker FAQ: 'Two USB-C/Thunderbolt ports are required on the MacBook for dual extended displays.'

findings.label: Extended displays by Apple chip
findings.value: M1/M2: 1 external (second monitor goes black); base M3: two extended with lid closed, mirroring with lid open; M4/M5 and Pro/Max: two extended
findings.note: From the maker FAQ and chart. M5 appears in the chart but not in the FAQ list.

findings.label: Price and charging, AV Access US store
findings.value: $289.99; up to 100 W to the MacBook
findings.note: Maker page price; DC 20 V/6 A supply.

findings.label: DP Alt Mode lane split vs USB data
findings.value: 2-lane mode: USB 3.2 Gen 2x1 (10 Gb/s) data plus one 4K60 or two 2560×1600 at 60 Hz; 4-lane mode: two 4K60 but USB 2.0 data only
findings.source_title: Exploring DisplayPort Alt Mode over USB-C (Newnex Technology)
findings.note: Newnex: the 2-lane mode is 'commonly adopted by USB-C docking stations'. Arithmetic: HBR3 is 8.1 Gb/s per lane, and 8b/10b coding gives 2 lanes = 12.96 Gb/s payload. One 3840×2160×60×24-bit stream is about 11.9 Gb/s of active pixels before blanking, so two streams (about 24 Gb/s or more) can't fit in 2 lanes without compression.

findings.label: Standard's own wording on lane sharing
findings.value: DP Alt Mode may use 1 or 2 of the 4 lanes so 'the other two lanes can be used for SuperSpeed USB data at the same time'
findings.source_title: VESA Brings DisplayPort to New USB Type-C Connector (VESA, 2014-09-22)
findings.note: VESA press release from when DP Alt Mode launched.

findings.label: Host requirement for dual 4K60 over one USB-C MST link
findings.value: DP 1.4 with DSC (or DP 2.1); DP 1.4 without DSC may lack bandwidth for dual 4K60; DP 1.2 typically limited to dual 1080p60
findings.source_title: Does My Laptop Support the Plugable UD-MSTH2? What to Check Before Buying (Plugable KB, updated 2026-08-28)
findings.note: Plugable is a dock maker writing about its own USB-C MST dock, so this is a maker statement but not AV Access's. It also says USB-C ports that list only data speed or charging don't confirm video support, and that macOS gives one extended display and one mirrored.

unsourced: Whether the iDock C20 and KD-E10 run their laptop USB-C link in 2-lane or 4-lane DP Alt Mode, and which MST hub chip they use. Not stated on the AV Access product pages, the iDock series page, or the manuals.plus listings in search results.
An AV Access statement that dual 4K60 on the C20 or KD-E10 needs DSC on the host. The maker pages require only DP Alt and MST.

Which laptop CPU or GPU generations output DP 1.4 DSC over USB-C. The StarTech MST14CD122DP page I opened had no host-requirement text; a search snippet citing Intel 12th gen wasn't opened, so it isn't used. The SIIG dock page returned HTTP 429.
Apple's own wording on MST support. Search found no support.apple.com page stating it, so the Mac findings rely on AV Access and Plugable.
